note: Six-layer sweep with the full LPADC device-PM fix set: the driver's TURN_ON reconfiguration and per-sequence hold, PM support in the NXP PORT pinctrl and VREF regulator drivers, the power-domain driver visiting every child on RESUME, the pm_system_resume() ordering fix, and the MCXA/MCXN default that puts the system timer's low-power companion (LPTMR through the Counter API) in the build. Images were flashed as .hex over dapeng remote and the console captured over the forwarded serial stream; each layer was checked for the sample's own RESULT line.

frdm_mcxn947/mcxn947/cpu0.note: All six layers pass. The two constraint checks in the system layer needed a sample fix, not a driver fix: pm_policy_state_lock_is_active() answers for the power state and not for one device, and under CONFIG_PM the console LPUART holds the same Deep Sleep and Power Down locks until its transmission-complete interrupt runs, so a sample taken straight after a printk() reported the console. Readings drift between phases (2519 down to 1688 raw) because the channel reads a floating pin; only conversion success is a pass criterion.

frdm_mcxa156/mcxa156.note: The four layers that stay out of Deep Sleep pass. The remaining two are blocked by an MCXA wake-up defect that has nothing to do with the LPADC: on this SoC a k_msleep() that lands in PM_STATE_SUSPEND_TO_IDLE never returns. Reproduced with a 20-line application holding no drivers at all (CONFIG_PM=y, three sleeps in a row): 20 ms in RUNTIME_IDLE returns, 60 ms in Deep Sleep does not. The same application on frdm_mcxn947 returns from RUNTIME_IDLE, Deep Sleep and Power Down alike, so the LPM companion timer is armed correctly there and the difference is in the MCXA wake path (the LPTMR is declared as a WUU module-6 wake-up source on both families).
